sources.title: Mark van de Logt, Ponca, Oklahoma Historical Society
sources.note: Full indexed institutional article read: agriculture, treaties, 1877 forced removal and southern settlement. Avoid differing exact dates for separation from Omaha and overly broad constitutional characterization of Standing Bear ruling.

sources.title: History Nebraska, The Ponca Villages
sources.note: Direct institutional marker text: earthlodges, maize and seasonal bison hunting.

sources.title: History Nebraska, Siouan Archeology
sources.note: Institutional summary of John R. Bozell research: Ponca Fort and Truteau trading post. Other villages on page belong to other peoples.

sources.title: James H. Howard, The Ponca Tribe (1965)
sources.note: Printed page 129, full indexed original. Reproducible query: "The Ponca tribe" Howard "games" "children". Recollections attributed to consultant PLC; no precise date assigned to the remembered practice.

sources.title: National Park Service, Chief Standing Bear
sources.note: Full indexed NPS text: son died December 1878, return January 1879, detention and May 12 habeas corpus ruling.

sources.title: Ponca Tribe of Oklahoma, Constitution
sources.note: Full indexed tribal constitution: approved May 23, 1950; adopted September 20, 1950, 129 votes to 24.

sources.title: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska, Northern Ponca Restoration Day
sources.note: Official history of 1966 termination and October 31, 1990 restoration; dates concern federal recognition, not existence of people.

sources.title: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska, June 2021 Member News
sources.note: Direct 20-page PDF text. Printed page 1 / PDF index 2 language by Angie Starkel; printed page 4 / PDF index 5 Earth Ambassadors contest. Exact ní / water; accent indicates stress.

sources.title: Ponca Tribe of Oklahoma, Water Department
sources.note: Direct official page, Water Supply and Treatment: alluvial aquifer connected to Salt Fork Arkansas River, wells, treatment and distribution. Undated changing population and construction claims omitted.

sources.title: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska, Buffalo Program
sources.note: Official program history: established 1994 through InterTribal Bison Cooperative grant; meat for powwow and elders. Changing herd size omitted.

sources.title: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska, Standing Bear’s pipe-tomahawk returned (2022)
sources.note: Direct June 15, 2022 report, paragraphs 1-3: provenance and June 3 return ceremony attended by both governments.

sources.title: Ponca Tribe of Oklahoma, Self-Governance
sources.note: Full indexed official text identifies participation since 1999 and federal program funding agreements.

sources.title: Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma, About Us and History of the Ioway
sources.note: Direct full tribal history: 1836 reservation, southern movement in 1878, executive order August 15, 1883 and distinct present governments. Internally varying name stories and problematic linguistic shorthand are not adopted.

sources.title: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska, About Us
sources.note: Direct text: 1854 territorial line, March 6, 1861 treaty boundaries, northern continuity, Oneota links shared with other peoples. Inconsistent population figures omitted.

sources.title: Chérie E. Haury-Artz, A River of Unrivaled Advantages
sources.note: University of Iowa Office of the State Archaeologist, direct PDF. Printed pages 20-22 / PDF indices 19-21: No-Heart map, Iowaville objects, geophysical survey and departure uncertainty. All pages counted as one work.

sources.title: William Green, Fur Trade Economics and Cultural Interaction at Iowaville, 1770-1810 (2002)
sources.note: Conference abstract, printed page 58. Full indexed original: deer hides, English firearms, pipestone sources and French-Indigenous family networks. Query: site.midwestarchaeology.org "Iowaville" "2002" "deer".

sources.title: University of Iowa, Archaeology Discovery Trunks
sources.note: Full indexed institutional teaching collection: Oneota period, shell-tempered pottery, bison-scapula hoes, maize/beans/squash. Material belongs to broad ancestral tradition, not exclusively Ioway.

sources.title: Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma, Oral History
sources.note: Direct text, opening paragraphs: elder interviews, audio, photographs, family history and winter Wa-Kah storytelling. Undated statements about current language classes omitted.

sources.title: Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma, January 2015 Newsletter
sources.note: Printed page 11, Chairman’s Interview: Bah Kho-Je Xla Chi (Grey Snow Eagle House). Full indexed original; direct extraction fails 11 MB size limit. Reproducible query: "January-2015-Newsletter.pdf" "Eagle". Modern institutional name, not precontact text.

sources.title: Grey Snow Eagle House, About Us
sources.note: Direct official account of January 2006 opening and rehabilitation, education, research and long-term care. Changing bird counts omitted.

sources.title: Grey Snow Eagle House, Rehabilitation and Long-Term Care
sources.note: Direct official page, Long-Term Care and Rehabilitation: rock bathing pools, enrichment, veterinary care and 150-foot flight cage with a turn.

sources.title: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska, Iowa and Sac & Fox Mission Museum
sources.note: Direct current official page: construction 1845-46; building and ten acres returned October 7, 2021. Use explicit prose date, not earlier inference from timeline ending in 2022.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Share people history with explicit northern/southern institutional scope, not interchangeable current governments.
batchIdentityNotes.decoded: ponca 1492-1783: Niobrara/Missouri country. ponca-oklahoma 1492-1500: north-central Oklahoma polygon, bbox [-97.2459724597246,36.50646362108898,-96.88596885968859,36.68065543151906].
batchIdentityNotes.limitation: Oklahoma outline is anachronistic at 1492; public overview says so. Preserve imported metadata as map coverage, not historical dating.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: OHS forced removal 1877; Oklahoma constitution and Nebraska restoration identify regional governments; joint 2022 return ceremony demonstrates common history without merging governments.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Share people history while distinguishing two current governments and later southern migration.
batchIdentityNotes.limitation: Small Oklahoma polygon cannot establish 1492 occupation by the later southern community. Public overview names the 1878/1883 mismatch. Original map dates remain coverage metadata.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: Both tribal governments describe shared Ioway identity and northern/southern division. Oklahoma history explicitly dates movement to 1878 and reservation to August 15, 1883.
